title: Chess, But SCP-966 Is Disturbed at Night...
summary: Halloween fog-of-war chess vs Stockfish. The board is covered in fog: you only see squares your own pieces can see/move to. SCP-966 ('the sleepless killer') wanders hidden in the fog (starts around c4) and every piece adjacent to it becomes a zombie - a neutral piece that no longer belongs to either side, moves on its own every round (all zombies simultaneously) and can capture any piece of either colour. SCP-966 can never move onto an occupied square, so the narrator walls it off with pawns to herd it into Black's camp, where the engine's pieces get zombified; Stockfish's queen then grabs zombie material, its king is exposed down the f-file and White wins.
rules: Fog of war for the player: only squares your pieces attack/can move to (plus your own pieces' squares) are visible; Stockfish plays normal chess.
SCP-966 is a neutral entity that moves one square per round; it can never move onto an occupied square; it is only visible when in your line of sight.
After SCP-966 moves, every piece (either colour) on one of its 8 adjacent squares becomes a zombie.
Zombies are neutral: they no longer belong to their side, you cannot move them, and they do not give you vision.

Each round all zombies move automatically and simultaneously, keeping their original piece movement (former white pawns still only move 'up', former black pawns 'down'); a newly zombified piece does not move on the turn it is zombified.
Zombies can capture any piece, of either colour; normal pieces can capture zombies.
Kings: adjacency rule presumably applies to kings too [not shown; inferred risk].
